title: Y-Sh-V

lines: A HUNTER, A MAN OF THE FIELD.
A PLAIN MAN, DWELLING IN TENTS.
cards: Two brothers, described in a single verse. "Esau was a cunning hunter, a man of the field; and Jacob was a plain man, dwelling in tents." One goes out.
One stays in. The Hebrew for dwelling there is yoshev: sitting. The rabbis didn't let that word pass.
In the midrash, and in Rashi after it, Jacob's tents become tents of study, and the quiet brother becomes a man sitting over his learning. Not much happens in that half of the verse. A man sits.
Today's root is the one under his seat, and under the word yeshiva.

teach.b: Y-Sh-V. Yod, shin, vet. Yashav: to sit, to dwell, to settle.
First, the yeshiva, the house of Torah study. The word is a sitting, a session: learning is something you do by staying put long enough. Second, the Shema.

teach.h: WHEN THOU SITTEST IN THINE HOUSE.
teach.b: It says to speak these words "when thou sittest in thine house, and when thou walkest by the way." Sitting at home comes first in the list: the chair, the table, the ordinary evening. Third, where you sit, and with whom.

teach.h: NOR SITTETH IN THE SEAT OF THE SCORNFUL.
teach.b: The first psalm blesses the one who walks not in the counsel of the ungodly, "nor sitteth in the seat of the scornful." Sitteth is yashav; seat is moshav, from the same letters.
And another psalm sings, "Behold, how good and how pleasant it is for brethren to dwell together in unity!" Dwell there is shevet, sitting. The root cares about the company you keep in your chair.
Fourth, settling. Yishuv is a settlement, a place people have put down roots.
And the rabbis speak of yishuv ha-da'at, a settled mind: the calm that lets a person think clearly before deciding. The same letters cover a village on a hillside and a mind that has stopped racing.
So the root makes an offer that sounds almost too simple.
Sit down. Stay. Let your thoughts land.
Then learn something, sitting where you are.

how: In a yeshiva, students sit for long sessions of Torah study, some of them in pairs; the Shema speaks of the words 'when thou sittest in thine house', and the rabbis prize yishuv ha-da'at, a settled mind, before learning or deciding.

o: the Hebrew root of sleeping and resting
the Hebrew root of sitting, dwelling, settling
the Hebrew root of saving and rescue

p: a sitting, a house of study

s: the Shema mentions sitting in your house
"when thou sittest in thine house, and when thou walkest by the way."
the first psalm blesses the one who sits in the seat of the scornful
the opposite: blessed is the man who doesn't, "nor sitteth in the seat of the scornful": yashav, and moshav, a seat.
yishuv can mean a settled mind
yishuv ha-da'at: the calm that lets a person think clearly.

games.q: two brothers. one is a hunter, a man of the field. what does the Torah say the other one does?
games.why: Jacob was "a plain man, dwelling in tents": yoshev, sitting. the midrash reads those tents as tents of study.

practice: Feel your seat hold you, feet on the floor, and let your thoughts land one at a time.

Then say one line slowly, perhaps the Shema's when thou sittest in thine house, and stay with it word by word without hurrying to the end; if a question comes, set it aside, it'll keep. If you pray, the line can be your prayer.

wordCard.voice: Y-Sh-V. Yod, shin, vet: yashav, to sit, to dwell, to settle. The yeshiva, and the settled mind. Today's word.

orig.note: Hebrew: a sitting, a house of study, from yod, shin, vet, to sit or dwell.

carryVoice: Your line: sit and learn. In Hebrew, a house of learning is named for sitting still. Till tomorrow.
